diagrams.title: GRC Artifacts Pyramid
diagrams.subtitle: Four categories, four different questions. Click a cell to see the exact role of each artifact.

cells.detail: A policy states a high-level intent, approved by leadership, that applies to the entire organization.
A standard sets a measurable, verifiable requirement: encryption, password length, baseline.
A procedure describes repeatable steps for a task: account revocation, restoration, runbook.

cells.text: Who does what in a crisis?
cells.detail: A plan organizes continuity or recovery: BCP for business operations, DRP for systems.
Enforceable across all personnel; its authority comes from executive approval, not publication.
Applicable and measurable: compliance can be verified through a control or scan.
Follows a validated sequence of steps to reduce improvisation under pressure.
Activated during a disruption; it defines roles, timelines, and resources.
Ten policies are listed in the objectives: AUP, BYOD, clean desk, information security, IR, classification/retention, access control, disposal, vulnerability disclosure, privacy.
The objectives also cite physical standards and RFCs as external references.
Standard operating procedures and execution guides for operations.
Business continuity plan and disaster recovery plan.
The baseline is compared against the actual system configuration.
The procedure is kept up to date when the environment changes.
An untested plan demonstrates no recovery capability.
